ai.description: This 5–9 cm frog is rotund and deep purple with a pale venter. It has a tiny, pointed head, a shovel-shaped snout, and small eyes, all adapted for a subterranean, fossorial lifestyle.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Purple Frog is uniquely identified by its globular, bloated body, tiny head, and pointed, pig-like snout, which distinguish it from all other Indian frog species.
ai.habitat: The purple frog inhabits the Western Ghats of India, living in moist deciduous and evergreen forests at elevations ranging from 50 to 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The purple frog spends most of its life underground, emerging briefly during monsoon rains to breed and forage for termites using its specialized, shovel-like limbs.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Purple Frog breeds during the pre-monsoon rains (May–June) in flowing streams, laying a clutch of 3,000–3,700 eggs in rock pools using external fertilization.
ai.distributionRemarks: The purple frog is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 50 and 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The purple frog emits a short, low-pitched, sheep-like bleat while calling from deep underground in moist, forested habitats during the monsoon season.
